extracted.intended_audience: Prospective authors submitting expository mathematics articles to Mathematics Magazine (teachers, undergraduate-level writers, and contributors of undergraduate-focused expository pieces).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting expository mathematics manuscripts aimed at undergraduate students and their instructors for publication in Mathematics Magazine, including stylistic, substantive, and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository style (clear and lively)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles should be written in a clear and lively expository style. The Magazine is not a research journal; papers in a terse "theorem-proof" style are unsuitable for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a context for the mathematics with examples, applications, illustrations, and historical background. The editors especially welcome papers with historical content and those that draw connections among branches of mathematics or to other disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contain interesting mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Every article should contain interesting mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles that are primarily on mathematical pedagogy alone or consist mainly of computer programs are unsuitable. The Magazine encourages articles that arise from undergraduate research or pose questions to inspire it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your work attractive and accessible to non-specialists, including well-prepared undergraduates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Magazine's intended audience is teachers of collegiate mathematics and their students; aim to provide stimulating supplements for undergraduate courses and to inform and refresh teachers by revealing new connections or offering new historical perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance exposition and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript's publishability depends as much on the quality of exposition as on mathematical significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Say something new in an appealing way, or say something old in a refreshing, new way. Say it clearly and directly, assuming a minimum of background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should check the novelty of their idea before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Magazine's searchable database of past pieces from Mathematics Magazine and the College Mathematics Journal to help verify novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vigorous, expressive, informal writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your writing vigorous, expressive, and informal, using the active voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give plenty of examples and minimize computation. Help the reader understand your motivation and share your insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrations and graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrate your ideas with visually appealing graphics, including figures, tables, drawings, and photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For initial submission, graphical material may be interspersed with text. Each figure should be numbered and referenced by number in the text. Authors are responsible for providing images of suitable quality; if accepted, supply separate copies of all illustrations both with and without added lettering, and electronic versions preferably in PostScript format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and opening paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a short, descriptive, and attractive title; opening sentences should provide a welcoming introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feel free to make the title funny if it would draw the reader in. Readers should know why they ought to invest time reading your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee expectations and revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees are asked to give detailed suggestions on style and check for mathematical accuracy; most papers require careful revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To shorten the revision process, read your work carefully (possibly after a cooling-off period). In the interest of referees' time, provide a referee's appendix (not for publication) that expands on suppressed statements such as 'A simple calculation shows...' to save referees time.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a generous list of references to invite further study; bibliographies may include suggested reading as well as cited sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite sources that are currently and readily available. List references either alphabetically or in the order cited, adhering closely to the Magazine's style for capitalization, italics, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article vs Note length and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Most papers are published either as Articles or as Notes; Articles have broader scope and usually run longer than 2000 words; Notes are shorter and more narrowly focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles should be divided into a few sections, each with a carefully chosen title. Notes usually need less formal sectioning. Footnotes and subsectioning are almost never used in the Magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable miscellany (other formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to expository pieces, the Magazine accepts a limited number of Math Bites, poems, cartoons, Proofs Without Words, and other miscellanea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation and LaTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors recommend using simple, unadorned LaTeX in manuscript preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should be generously spaced, with the title, author, and author's address at the top of the first page. Templates for Articles and Notes (in .tex and .pdf) are available. Number the pages, and number only those equations that you refer to in the text. Whether LaTeX is used or not, the editors hope for some electronic version of every accepted article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic complements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may provide electronic complements to their article (color illustrations, Java applets, animations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply the URL of a draft site for any electronic complement; if the article is accepted, complements will be hosted on the Magazine's site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure and copies required
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission requires multiple hard copies and full contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please submit three copies and provide full contact information including email. In cases of multiple authorship specify one corresponding author. Direct correspondence to the Editor (Allen J. Schwenk) at the Department of Mathematics, Western Michigan University. Electronic submission is possible in limited circumstances; ultimately two hard copies are needed to send to referees and one to retain. To request that the editors do printing for you, inquire at math-mag@wmich.edu or by phone (269-387-4532).
